summary: Fairwood tree lookout on two cut trees, built by Fred Fraser and used until about 1950; the summit is now in Spring Lake/Lake Desire Park and no remains are described.

facts.design: Platform on two trees cut off about 50 feet up, with two adjoining trees as a ladder and a tent at the base
facts.status_note: Used until about 1950; no source we read describes what, if anything, remains of the platform

access.note: Inside Spring Lake/Lake Desire Park; the summit is reached by a hiker-only Summit Trail, and a private home sits just below the summit

visit.trail_note: Distance 1.2 miles and elevation gain 400 feet, from the southeast trailhead (Willhite)

events.note: Used until about 1950 per the register and Willhite; neither gives a build year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Willhite's text both describe a platform on two cut trees, so they agree on a tree lookout. Only Willhite's 1940s photo caption uses the word station, and the text does not explain it.

sources.title: Spring Lake/Lake Desire Park and McGarvey Park

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register and Forest Lookouts pages are short, Willhite is a hiking site with photo captions, and King County covers the park. No source gives a build year, so the events list has no built event. The record's elevation of 273 m matches the register's 896 ft. The LOOKOUT rock caption and the park trail facts come from a hiking site's photo caption and the county park page, not from a recent site visit. The brief's conflict note (tower, building or only a tree) resolves toward a tree lookout; the station wording is one photo caption. Used 1 WebSearch and about 8 page reads, over the per-tower budget, mainly re-reading the Willhite page for its full text.
